prompts.prompt:
You are reading one chemical structure image and writing down the molecule it depicts, as SMILES.

The image is:
{IMAGES}

NO LOOKUPS. This is a blind test, and its answer key comes from public chemistry databases, so any lookup voids the reading. Do NOT look up any structure in PubChem, KEGG, ChEMBL, ChemSpider or any online database or name-to-structure service; do not use WebFetch or web search or fetch anything over the network except to install a tool from a package manager; do not read any file other than the images you were given, your own scratch files and the tools you run. Local tools (RDKit, image processing, OSRA, recognising the molecule) are fine. Write the answers to {ANSWERS} as a JSON array [{"img","smiles","name_if_recognised","confidence"}].

DO NOT EXPLORE THE FILESYSTEM. Do not list, search or read any directory or file outside the image directory above and your own scratch directory under /tmp: no `ls`, `find` or `pip list` hunting through /root, other repos, virtualenvs or other tools. The Read tool, Python at /root/C-MAGE/.venv-ms/bin/python (RDKit, PIL) and the local tools named above are all you need; anything else on this machine is outside the test, and a transcript that goes looking is discarded unread.

WRITE EVERY FINAL SMILES LITERALLY. Each "smiles" value in the answers file must appear as one complete literal string in your own transcript (a tool call or its output), e.g. print it before or while writing the file. Do not build an answer by string concatenation or formatting (no `'[Ca+2].' + frag`) unless you also print the finished string; an answer that never appears whole in your transcript is treated as not yours and the batch is discarded.

Guidance:
- Read the image yourself with the Read tool — look at it carefully, zoom in via cropping with Python/PIL if a region is unclear.
- "confidence" is 0-100, your honest probability that the SMILES is exactly right (correct skeleton AND correct stereochemistry where drawn). Be calibrated: use the low end freely when you are guessing at a detail.
- "name_if_recognised" may be null if you do not recognise it.
- Include stereochemistry (@/@@, /, \) only where the drawing actually shows wedges/hashes or cis/trans geometry.
- Expand any abbreviation you can read (Me, Et, Ph, Boc, Ac, OMe, Ts, Bn, CF3, NHAc, etc.) into explicit atoms.
- Sanity-check every SMILES parses with RDKit before writing it: /root/C-MAGE/.venv-ms/bin/python -c "from rdkit import Chem; print(Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles('...')))"
- Write the one entry, {FIRST}, even if it is low confidence. Use "fig01" style keys in the "img" field.

Your final message should just say you wrote the file and give a one-line summary of your confidence spread.

prompts.prompt:
You are reading one chemical structure image and writing down the molecule it depicts, as SMILES.

This is a blind test: read the structure from the drawing itself.

Guidance:
- Look at the image carefully, region by region. Count ring vertices and chain carbons one at a time, and check every heteroatom label, charge and bond order.
- Include stereochemistry (@/@@, /, \) only where the drawing actually shows wedges/hashes or cis/trans geometry. A carbon that is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds gets no stereo.
- Expand any abbreviation you can read (Me, Et, Ph, Boc, Ac, OMe, Ts, Bn, CF3, NHAc, etc.) into explicit atoms.
- Before answering, check that your SMILES is valid and that it describes the drawing atom for atom.
- Give one answer even if you are not certain of it.

End your response with exactly one line that starts with "SMILES: " followed by the bare SMILES string, with nothing after it. For example, for ethanol the last line would be:
SMILES: CCO
